name: MG Marg
tagline: The pedestrianised main street, benches and no litter
description: Gangtok's central promenade, closed to vehicles, paved and lined with shops, cafes and hotels, with benches down the middle and a strictly enforced no-litter and no-smoking rule that is genuinely observed. It is the town's living room and where the evening walk happens.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the shops, cafes and the evening promenade on foot
pros: All shops, cafes and services along it
cons: Busy with domestic tourists in season
Everything is up or down a hill from it

name: Development Area and Deorali
tagline: Below the centre, quieter and better value
description: The districts stepping down the ridge south of MG Marg towards Deorali, with residential buildings, the ropeway station and the Institute of Tibetology among the pines below. Rents fall as you descend and the views out over the valley open up, though the climb back is real.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting lower rents and a valley view
pros: Views out over the Ranipool valley
Institute of Tibetology and the chorten nearby
cons: A steep climb back up to MG Marg
Taxis needed more often than you expect

name: Tadong and the University Side
tagline: North along the ridge, students and local prices
description: The district north of the centre towards Sikkim University and the government colleges, with student accommodation, local shops and a young population. Rents are the lowest in Gangtok and it has none of the tourist pricing that shapes the centre.
bestFor: Budget stays wanting local prices and a student circle
pros: The lowest rents in the town
Local shops and food at ordinary prices
Young population and a genuine local neighbourhood

name: Rumtek (24 km southwest)
tagline: Across the valley at the monastery
description: The village around Rumtek Monastery, seat of the Karmapa and one of the most important Tibetan Buddhist institutions outside Tibet, on a ridge across the valley from Gangtok. A handful of guesthouses serve visitors and practitioners. It is quiet, high and entirely oriented around the monastery.
bestFor: Stays connected to the monastery or wanting genuine quiet
pros: Rumtek Monastery and its shedra on the doorstep
Views back across the valley to Gangtok
cons: An hour by road from Gangtok despite the distance
Almost no services and weak connectivity
Little to do beyond the monastery

name: Pelling and West Sikkim (110 km west)
tagline: The Kanchenjunga viewpoint and the old capitals
description: The western hill town that has the clearest and closest views of Kanchenjunga in Sikkim, with the ruins of Rabdentse, the state's second capital, and Pemayangtse Monastery nearby. It is smaller and quieter than Gangtok and the mountain views are the reason anyone goes.
bestFor: Stays where seeing Kanchenjunga every clear morning is the point
pros: The best Kanchenjunga views in the state
cons: Four to five hours by road from Gangtok
Very limited services and slow connectivity
Views depend entirely on the weather
